ORDER BY resistance_edges DESC, resistant_gene_count DESC
LIMIT 50

arguments.sql_query: SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='omop' AND table_name IN ('drug_exposure_extension','condition_occurrence_extension','observation_extension','procedure_occurrence_extension') ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position
SELECT TOP 50 stop_reason, COUNT(*) AS n FROM omop.drug_exposure WHERE stop_reason IS NOT NULL AND LTRIM(RTRIM(stop_reason)) <> '' GROUP BY stop_reason ORDER BY n DESC

SELECT TOP 100 c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.domain_id, c.vocabulary_id, c.concept_class_id, c.standard_concept, COUNT(*) AS n FROM omop.observation o JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id=o.observation_concept_id WHERE LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%treatment%' AND (LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%change%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%switch%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%adjust%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%modif%') GROUP BY c.concept_id,c.concept_name,c.domain_id,c.vocabulary_id,c.concept_class_id,c.standard_concept ORDER BY n DESC

SELECT TOP 100 c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.domain_id, c.vocabulary_id, c.concept_class_id, c.standard_concept, COUNT(*) AS n FROM omop.procedure_occurrence p JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id=p.procedure_concept_id WHERE LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%treatment%' AND (LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%change%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%switch%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%adjust%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%modif%') GROUP BY c.concept_id,c.concept_name,c.domain_id,c.vocabulary_id,c.concept_class_id,c.standard_concept ORDER BY n DESC

Using the MedCP KG + local OMOP data:

- The KG did **not** expose class-specific antimicrobial `RESISTANT_TO` edges; those edges were mostly oncology drugs. The usable KG resistance signal was organism-level `has_amr_phenotype=yes` — 86,207 AMR organisms, led by *S. pneumoniae*, *M. tuberculosis*, *K. pneumoniae*, *N. gonorrhoeae*, *E. faecium*, *E. coli*, and *S. aureus*.
- I therefore measured prescribing for major systemic antibacterial ATC classes and looked for SNOMED observation `Treatment changed` (`concept_id=40483850`) within 7 days of each drug exposure.

| Rank | Antimicrobial class | Prescriptions | Patients | Treatment changed ≤7d | % exposures |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Other beta-lactams incl. cephalosporins/carbapenems | 3,230,257 | 363,124 | 49 | 0.002% |
| 2 | Other antibacterials | 1,482,467 | 152,178 | 18 | 0.001% |
| 3 | Beta-lactam penicillins | 1,330,695 | 178,755 | 16 | 0.001% |
| 4 | Quinolones | 1,028,557 | 87,366 | 30 | 0.003% |
| 5 | Sulfonamides/trimethoprim | 941,332 | 83,038 | 53 | 0.006% |
| 6 | Macrolides/lincosamides/streptogramins | 685,476 | 97,280 | 17 | 0.002% |
| 7 | Tetracyclines | 501,120 | 81,285 | 9 | 0.002% |

Bottom line: locally, beta-lactams dominate prescribing among AMR-relevant antibacterial classes. Explicit “treatment changed” coding within 7 days is extremely rare across all classes, highest proportionally for sulfonamides/trimethoprim but still only 0.006%, so this code likely undercaptures real therapy switches.
